venue.name: Abkhazi Garden
venue.description: Abkhazi Garden is a one-acre heritage home and garden in Victoria, created by Prince and Princess Abkhazi from 1946 and owned since 2000 by The Land Conservancy of British Columbia. Visitors walk a concrete and gravel path through a rhododendron woodland, past three ponds set in glaciated rock, to a restored 1946 summerhouse and the house terrace. Admission is by a suggested donation of $10 per person. The Teahouse in the heritage house is a separate business from TLC.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The Teahouse at Abkhazi Garden is wheelchair accessible, however many of the pathways throughout the Garden are gravel or have steps that may be physically challenging for those with mobility issues.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking on the street is available, preferably on the north side of Fairfield Road, adjacent to the garden. Please do not park in the spaces marked 'Residential Parking Only'.

restrictions: Dogs are allowed in the Garden provided they are on leash and cleaned up after.
Please do not park in the spaces marked 'Residential Parking Only'.
venue.hours_notes: Summer Hours (April 1 – September 30): open 7 days a week from 11am to 5pm with the last entrance at 4pm. Winter Hours (October 1 – March 31): open Wednesday through Sunday from 11am to 5pm, last entrance at 4pm. Open on most statutory holidays; closed Christmas Day (December 25) and New Years Day (January 1).
venue.seasonal_notes: Abkhazi Garden plant sales are open 7 days a week from 11am to 4pm during the summer season.

programs.name: Self-guided garden visit
programs.description: The garden is open to the public with admission by a suggested donation of $10 per person, which goes to TLC's operation and maintenance of the garden. It is open 7 days a week from April 1 to September 30 and Wednesday to Sunday from October 1 to March 31, with last entrance at 4pm. The site does not publish any guided tour, group rate, group booking route or minimum age for children's groups.
programs.what_children_do: Walk a looping concrete and gravel path from the rhododendron woodland, across the south lawn and along the heather-lined path beside a large rock outcrop, with detours to three small ponds where mallard ducks live. The route climbs to the summerhouse and the house terrace, and at the garden shed the path divides into a most-even route and a steeper, rockier one.
programs.our_note: The whole visit is a walk over rock with steps, slopes and gravel, so it is slow with strollers and tiring for under-fives; at the garden shed, keep straight for the most even path to the house. Nothing about groups, group rates or a booking contact is on the site, so call TLC before you bring a class.
programs.practical_summary: The address, hours and a suggested $10 donation are published, and the garden is outdoors with gravel paths and steps. Washrooms, an indoor lunch space, rain backup, bus parking and any group rate are not stated anywhere — worth a call before you book.
programs.evidence: Admission is by a suggested donation of $10 per person
